  • (with rising pitch) Used to express [[:doubt#English|doubt]] or [[:confusion#English|confusion]]. #:
    '''Huh?''' Where did they go?
    [[Category:English terms with usage examples|HUH]] # (with falling pitch) Used to express [[:amusement#English|amusement]] or subtle [[:surprise#English|surprise]]. #:
    '''Huh!''' I'm sure I locked it when I left.
    [[Category:English terms with usage examples|HUH]] # (with rising pitch) Used to [[:reinforce#English|reinforce]] a [[:question#English|question]]. #:
    Where were you last night? '''Huh'''?
    [[Category:English terms with usage examples|HUH]] # ([[Appendix:Glossary#slang|slang]][[Category:English slang|HUH]], with falling pitch) Used either to [[:belittle#English|belittle]] the issuer of a statement/question, or [[:sarcasm#English|sarcastically]] to indicate utter agreement, and that the statement being responded to is an extreme [[:understatement#English|understatement]]. The intonation is changed to distinguish between the two meanings - implied [[:dullness#English|dullness]] for belittlement, and [[:feigned#English|feigned]] [[:surprise#English|surprise]] for utter agreement. #:
    (belittlement) A: "We should go to an amusement park; it would be fun." B: "'''Huh.'''"
    [[Category:English terms with usage examples|HUH]] #:
    (agreement) A: "Murder is bad." B: "'''Huh!'''"
    [[Category:English terms with usage examples|HUH]] # ([[Appendix:Glossary#informal|informal]][[Category:English informal terms|HUH]], with rising pitch) Used to indicate that one did not hear what was said. #: Synonyms: [[:come again#English|come again]], [[:pardon#English|pardon]], [[:what#English|what]]; ''see also'' [[Thesaurus:say again#English|Thesaurus:say again]] #:

    [[Category:English terms with usage examples|HUH]] # ([[Appendix:Glossary#informal|informal]][[Category:English informal terms|HUH]], with falling pitch) Used to create a [[:tag question#English|tag question]]. #:
